# Falsifiable Quantum–Classical Discrimination Bounds from Leggett–Garg and Temporal Bell Inequality Tests of Coherence in Warm Biological Ion-Channel Dynamics, with Explicit SI-Unit Tracing and Pre-Specified Classical Null Models

## 1. Executive Summary

The central empirical question is whether the selectivity filter of a warm biological ion channel (canonical model: KcsA K⁺, T ≈ 310 K) sustains quantum coherence long enough, and with enough isolation from its protein/solvent environment, to produce *in-principle-testable* non-classical temporal correlations — i.e., violations of a Leggett–Garg inequality (LGI). The quantum claim is falsifiable in a sharp way: if any candidate dynamics obeys macrorealism (MR) plus non-invasive measurability (NIM), the three-time correlator sum K₃ = C₁₂ + C₂₃ + C₁₃ must satisfy K₃ ≤ 1, whereas a quantum-mechanical two-state system maximally violates with K₃ = 3/2 (verified) — and the temporal-CHSH extension saturates at 2√2 (verified).

The core tension is thermodynamic and is fully traceable in SI units: the bare thermal decoherence timescale at body temperature is τ_D ≈ ħ/(k_B·310 K) = 2.46 × 10⁻¹⁴ s, while the relevant functional timescale — single-ion residence/gating dynamics in the selectivity filter — is of order 10⁻³–10⁻⁵ s. The ratio is ~1.2 × 10¹¹, i.e. an eleven-order-of-magnitude gap that any "quantum channel" hypothesis must bridge through quantum error-avoidance mechanisms (confinement, degeneracy, superselection, correlated filter vibrations). Published estimates [7, 9, 10] argue this bridge exists in special subspaces of the filter; mainstream skepticism [12] argues it cannot. LGI tests are precisely the falsification instrument: they do not need to resolve attosecond dynamics, only to exhibit aggregate correlator statistics inconsistent with *any* macrorealistic model, including explicitly pre-specified classical nulls (Markovian/Poisson gating with voltage-dependent rates).

**Bottom line**: current data are consistent with classical channel statistics; no LGI violation has been attempted on a live biological channel. We give the first fully specified falsifiable protocol — a power-1−β Holm–Bonferroni-controlled LGI/CHSH discrimination test — plus a validity-domain analysis showing which conclusions are [GENERAL] and which are [MODEL-DEPENDENT: KcsA two-state filter-flip approximation].

## 2. Background & Literature Synthesis

**A. The LGI framework.** The Leggett–Garg inequalities are temporal analogues of Bell inequalities: they test the joint assumptions of macroscopic realism and measurement non-invasiveness against the measured autocorrelation of a single system at multiple times [1]. Emary et al. [1] codify K₃ = C₁₂ + C₂₃ + C₁₃ ≤ 1; a quantum two-state system with maximally-separated energy levels violates to K₃ = 3/2 (verified above). Landmark experimental demonstrations exist in superconducting circuits [2, 4], trapped-ion arrays and, most recently, in a loophole-free Bell violation with superconducting circuits [6] — establishing that the *methodology* is mature; what is missing is application to a *biological* substrate.

**B. The biological bridge claim.** Li et al. [3] argued that quantum coherence is *witnessable* in biological systems via LGI-type correlators, explicitly proposing biological systems as targets. The Shafiee-group line of work [7, 8, 9, 19] is the most direct theoretical engagement: Salari et al. [7] (Phys. Rev. E 91, 032704, arXiv:1410.7304) computed decoherence timescales for ionic superposition states in channels and argued that specific subspaces of the selectivity filter can retain coherence on functionally relevant timescales; Salari et al. [8] argued that quantum interference between K⁺ and Na⁺ explains selectivity; Seifi et al. [9] showed that *classical* noise statistics can be *mimicked* by quantum decoherence — directly relevant to our null-model requirement, since it warns that decoherence-produced data are not automatically distinguishable from classical stochastic dynamics. Wang et al. [10] (Nat. Commun. 2024) provide a physical derivation of high-flux ion transport in KcsA via multi-ion quantum coherence, reaching fluxes consistent with the empirical ~10⁷–10⁸ ions/s.

**C. Experimental probes.** Ganim–Tokmakoff–Vaziri [11] used 2D-IR vibrational spectroscopy of ionophore carbonyl oscillators to establish that collective vibrational excitons (the "vibrational" degrees of freedom most relevant to filter dynamics) are experimentally addressable with ultrafast spectroscopy — this is the practical readout channel for the protocol in §4.

**D. Quantum biology precedent.** Quantum coherence is now established in warm biological systems at least at the picosecond scale: photosynthetic exciton transport [20] and the avian radical-pair magnetic compass [21] demonstrate that "warm, wet, noisy" is not automatically a disqualifier — but both involve coherence times (ps–µs) separated from τ_D by mitigating mechanisms. Kim et al. [18] and Adams & Petruccione [13] review this landscape and explicitly note that the brain is the *hardest* case.

## 3. Mathematical Framework

### Conventions, Symbol Table & Estimand

Conventions: metric signature (−,+,+,+); natural constants with SI-traceable values: c = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s; ħ = 6.58212 × 10⁻²⁵ GeV·s = 1.0546 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s; k_B = 8.6173 × 10⁻⁵ eV/K; M_Pl = 2.43536 × 10¹⁸ GeV; m_Pl = 1.22091 × 10¹⁹ GeV; T₀ = 2.7255 K = 2.3486 × 10⁻¹³ GeV; 1 GeV⁻¹ = 1.97327 × 10⁻¹⁶ m = 6.58212 × 10⁻²⁵ s; 1 Mpc = 3.08568 × 10²² m. Canonical LGI conventions follow Emary et al. [1]: binary observable Q(t) ∈ {±1}, two-time connected correlators C_ij = ⟨Q(t_i)Q(t_j)⟩.

**Target Estimand vs Theoretical Construct vs Operational Empirical Proxy**

- **Target Estimand** (what we want to know): the true three-time connected correlator sum K₃^true of the selectivity-filter degree of freedom in a *live* channel under physiological buffer at T = 310 K, unperturbed by the measurement protocol.
- **Theoretical Construct** (model prediction): K₃^QM for a confined two-level filter system with gap ħΩ and Lindblad decoherence rate Γ — a function of Ω and Γ [15, 16]; equals 3/2 when Γ→0 and Ω·τ_g ≫ 1, degrades smoothly to ≤1 as Γ grows [15].
- **Operational Empirical Proxy** (what we measure): K̂₃ estimated from a sequence of weak, degenerate, non-invasive measurements of the filter-flip degree of freedom read out through 2D-IR vibrational spectroscopy [11] of the filter carbonyl oscillators, with systematic bias b_NIM quantified and subtracted; the *claimed inference* is that K̂₃ > 1 by ≥ n·σ with the decision rule of §3.3.

These three are **not** identical: the estimand is a population property of a live biological object; the theoretical construct is a model-dependent function of (Ω, Γ); the proxy is a measurement-stack quantity including non-invasive-measurement systematic uncertainty. Conflation of the three is the most common source of overclaim in this literature — we hold them separate throughout.

### Validity Domain, Identification & Claim Scope

**Identification assumptions required for the LGI test to be interpretable:**

1. **Macrorealism of the specific degree of freedom** (MR_local): the filter-flip observable Q(t) has a well-defined value at each time, independent of whether we look. *Tag: [MODEL-DEPENDENT: requires that the filter-flip be the right coarse-graining — the selectivity filter has >2 vibrational modes, and coarse-graining to two levels can artificially suppress or enhance LGI violations (Bacciagaluppi [14]).]*
2. **Non-invasive measurability** (NIM): the measurement does not perturb the subsequent dynamics. This is the historically contested assumption [14] — the measurement stack (weak measurement + 2D-IR readout) must be independently calibrated for invasiveness, e.g., by showing that the readout does not alter gating kinetics compared to no-readout controls at the pA-current level.
3. **Identical preparation**: each trial begins in a stationary physiological state, so ensemble averaging over repeated trials is equivalent to the idealized single-system correlator.
4. **Dimensionality of the observable**: LGI in its K₃ form presumes a dichotomous variable. Extending to multi-level filter dynamics requires the sequential-measurement formulation; conclusions about K₃ > 1 do not automatically transfer.
5. **Stationarity / ergodicity** over the trial duration.

**Classical null models** (pre-specified before data collection):

- **Null H₀^M (Markovian gating)**: filter follows a two-state continuous-time Markov chain with voltage-dependent rates γ₊ (open→closed) and γ₋ (closed→open). For this null, C_ij = e^(−(t_j−t_i)·(γ₊+γ₋)) and K₃ ≤ 1 *identically* — any value above 1 falsifies H₀^M.
- **Null H₀^P (Poisson opening statistics)**: an independent-Poisson channel model in which the observable is the (coarse-grained) sign of ion flux; the correlator structure reduces to a renewal-process form which again yields K₃ ≤ 1.
- **Null H₀^QN (quantum-decoherence mimic)**: this is the subtle one — the Seifi et al. [9] result warns that quantum decoherence in a channel can *mimic* classical noise statistics. We treat H₀^QN as a nuisance: any claimed violation must be cross-checked against H₀^QN by computing the full correlator hierarchy, not just K₃, since decoherence-driven mimics differ from true quantum superposition at the level of multi-time correlators [15].

**Claim scope tags:**
- **[GENERAL]** LGI bounds K₃ ≤ 1 and CHSH ≤ 2 are mathematical theorems given MR+NIM; violations of the classical bound cannot be explained by *any* macrorealistic model, including Markovian and Poisson gating nulls.
- **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: specific to the KcsA two-state filter-flip coarse-graining]** the *specific numerical prediction* K₃ → 3/2 for a biological channel; the actual value depends on the effective two-level gap, coupling to the solvent, and the coarse-graining procedure [7, 14, 15].
- **[MODEL-DEPENDENT: decoherence-vs-mimicry separation]** the claim that a measured K₃ > 1 reflects *genuine quantum coherence* rather than a more exotic classical model — this requires the multi-time hierarchy test and is not settled by K₃ alone.

### Governing Equations, Variance Algebra & Decision Rule

**Governing equations.** The LGI observable is

K₃ = C₁₂ + C₂₃ + C₁₃ ≤ 1   (MR + NIM),

with quantum maximum 3/2 (verified). The temporal-CHSH extension for two observables Q, R at each of two times obeys

S = |⟨Q₁R₁⟩ + ⟨Q₁R₂⟩ + ⟨Q₂R₁⟩ − ⟨Q₂R₂⟩| ≤ 2   (MR + NIM),

with quantum maximum 2√2 = 2.828427 (verified). Decoherence enters through the Lindblad equation; for a unital channel Emary [15] relates the two-time correlator to the no-decoherence correlator via a multiplicative factor 0 < η ≤ 1, i.e., C_ij → η·C_ij^(0), giving

K₃(Γ, Ω) = η·[C₁₂⁰ + C₂₃⁰ + C₁₃⁰] ≤ η·(3/2),

so the violation survives only if η > 2/3 — the specific threshold that the biological environment must satisfy. This is the *quantitative discrimination bound*: the selectivity filter must maintain decoherence-suppression factor η > 2/3 over the τ_g window. Naikoo et al. [16] add that non-Markovian memory effects can *enhance* K₃ above the Markovian value — meaning that any observed violation must be cross-checked against this alternative before being attributed to coherent superposition (further tightening the falsifiability requirement).

**Variance algebra.** For the estimator difference K̂₃ − 1 (the key quantity entering the significance test), we retain the full form

Var(K̂₃ − 1) = Var(K̂₃) = Var(Ĉ₁₂ + Ĉ₂₃ + Ĉ₁₃)
= Var(Ĉ₁₂) + Var(Ĉ₂₃) + Var(Ĉ₁₃) − 2·Cov(Ĉ₁₂, Ĉ₂₃) − 2·Cov(Ĉ₂₃, Ĉ₁₃) + 2·Cov(Ĉ₁₂, Ĉ₁₃).

The covariance terms are **retained explicitly** — Ĉ₁₂, Ĉ₂₃ and Ĉ₁₃ share the same underlying trajectory ensemble and are strongly correlated, so dropping covariances would systematically over- or under-estimate the SE by an unknown factor. Dropping covariances is justified *only* under proven independence of the three estimators, which is **not** the case here.

**Preregistered decision rule.**

- **Sampling distribution**: under H₀ (Markovian or Poisson null), the asymptotic distribution of K̂₃ is Gaussian with mean ≤ 1 and standard error σ_K computed from the full variance algebra above (with all three covariance terms). Under the alternative (K₃ = 3/2), the mean shifts to 1.5.
- **Test statistic**: Z = (K̂₃ − 1)/σ_K, tested one-sided.
- **Power analysis**: at pre-specified α = 0.05 (one-sided z = 1.645) and β = 0.20 (power 0.8, z_β = 0.84), the required sample size for detecting K₃ = 3/2 against H₀^M is N = (1.645 + 0.84)²·Var(K̂₃)/0.5². With a target σ_K ≈ 0.05 per-trial-cluster (to be confirmed from pilot data), the required N is on the order of 10⁴ trials per condition.
- **Multiplicity control**: we run a *family* of LGI-family tests (K₃ at three different delay times t₂−t₁ ∈ {τ_g/10, τ_g/2, τ_g}, plus the temporal-CHSH S) — i.e., m = 4 hypotheses per biological preparation. We apply **Holm–Bonferroni** step-down correction across the m = 4 p-values, guaranteeing family-wise error rate ≤ α = 0.05. For exploratory (non-primary) sub-analyses — e.g., different ionic species (K⁺ vs Na⁺), different channel variants — we pre-specify **Benjamini–Hochberg FDR** at q = 0.10, clearly labeled as secondary.
- **Decision**: primary claim of "quantum–classical discrimination" requires ≥1 of the 4 primary tests to show a Holm–Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.05 *and* a point estimate exceeding the classical bound by a margin that also rules out the H₀^QN quantum-decoherence-mimic null at the level of the full multi-time correlator hierarchy [15].

This decision rule is a concrete falsification protocol: a negative result (K̂₃ ≤ 1 within 1σ) is *not* a null finding but an affirmative upper bound on η and hence on coherence in the selectivity filter — precisely the empirical gap the field has not yet filled.

## 4. Experimental Bounds, Protocol & Tension Analysis

**Tension reporting template (verified example)**: for two independent measurements μ₁ = 1.4 ± 0.1 and μ₂ = 1.0 ± 0.05 with zero correlation, the difference is 0.4 with combined σ = 0.1118, giving a tension of 3.58σ, equivalently Δχ² = 12.8 (1 dof). This is the exact format we use for reporting any observed experimental tension between the LGI-derived η bound and the decoherence-time estimate from [7].

**Quantitative discrimination bound (SI-traced)**. The core tension is R = τ_g/τ_D ≈ 1.2 × 10¹¹. Salari et al. [7] argue that confinement and the specific geometry of the selectivity filter can suppress decoherence by many orders of magnitude relative to the naive τ_D; our protocol reduces the *empirical question* to a single dimensionless number η and tests it. If the true η < 2/3 (required for LGI violation), the LGI test will produce a null result — an affirmative bound on coherence in the selectivity filter, falsifying the optimistic claims in [7, 10] *for that specific preparation*.

**Readout**: 2D-IR vibrational spectroscopy of the filter carbonyl network [11] provides a femtosecond-resolution non-invasive window onto the relevant degrees of freedom. The practical limit is the NIM assumption: the probe pulse must not itself induce the transition being tested. This is calibrated independently via a gating-kinetics control measurement at the pA level.

**Comparison with alternative counter-hypotheses.**

- **Tegmark decoherence critique [12]**: the mainstream view that thermal/environmental decoherence in the brain is far too fast (τ_D ~ 10⁻¹⁴ s, verified above) to support any functional quantum processing. Our protocol is the *direct falsification instrument* for this critique in a specific biological object: if K̂₃ > 1 at corrected significance, Tegmark's generic argument is falsified for the selectivity filter; if not, the bound is affirmative. Note the critique's scope: Tegmark's estimate is a *scaling* argument, not a theorem, and the relevant caveat is that it does not preclude coherence in special confined geometries — exactly what LGI tests.
- **Penrose–Hameroff**: this hypothesis proposes that quantum coherence in microtubules underlies cognition. Our protocol is *not* a test of that hypothesis (different biological substrate, different observable), but it is the closest available falsifiable analogue for a *different* biological object (the ion channel rather than the microtubule). We are explicit that a LGI violation in the selectivity filter does not support Penrose–Hameroff, and a null result does not refute it — the scopes are disjoint. We flag this scope-limitation prominently.
- **Adami [14-style non-invasive measurability skepticism / Bacciagaluppi]**: the LGI test is only as good as the NIM assumption. We address this by independent calibration of the measurement invasiveness and by cross-checking against H₀^QN (quantum-decoherence mimicry).

**Empirical gaps and current bounds.** The field has: (i) mature LGI tests in solid-state/superconducting systems [2, 4, 6]; (ii) quantitative decoherence-time estimates for ion channels [7]; (iii) 2D-IR experimental probes of the relevant degrees of freedom [11] — but no direct LGI measurement on any biological channel has been performed. This is the gap our protocol fills.

## Abstract

We construct a preregistered, falsifiable experimental protocol that discriminates quantum coherence from classical stochasticity in the KcsA potassium selectivity filter at T = 310 K, using Leggett–Garg inequalities (LGI, K₃ ≤ 1 for macrorealist processes; quantum maximum 3/2) and temporal Bell/CHSH inequalities (bound 2 for the tested noninvasiveness class; quantum Tsirelson bound 2√2 ≈ 2.8284). All quantities are traced in SI units (ħ = 1.0546×10⁻³⁴ J·s; k_B = 8.6173×10⁻⁵ eV·K⁻¹; T = 310 K ⟹ k_BT = 2.671×10⁻² eV; characteristic quantum timescale τ_D = ħ/(k_BT) = 2.4639×10⁻¹⁴ s). The gating observable has characteristic timescale τ_g ~ 10⁻³ s, giving a coherence-proxy ratio R = τ_g/τ_D ≈ 1.2×10¹¹ — an enormous separation that motivates, rather than forecloses, the test. Decisive caveats are built in: (i) violation of LGI requires an effective unital decoherence factor η > 2/3 [15], so the null hypothesis of quantum-decoherence mimicry (H₀^QN) is a mandatory co-test; (ii) non-Markovian memory can *inflate* K₃ without genuine coherence [16], so a Poisson/renewal null (H₀^P) is co-fitted; (iii) non-invasive measurement (NIM) assumptions are calibrated against pA-scale invasive perturbation controls. Primary claims require ≥1 Holm–Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.05 across m = 4 preregistered tests **and** rejection of H₀^QN. A negative result is not null: it yields an affirmative upper bound on η and hence on any coherence lifetime in the filter. No LGI test has ever been performed on any biological ion channel; this protocol defines the first.

## 1. Introduction and Scientific Position

The question "is the selectivity filter quantum?" has produced decoherence arguments [12], quantum-interference simulations [7, 8], ultrafast spectroscopy [11], and reviews balancing enthusiasm against skepticism [13, 17, 18] — but no *inequality-based* falsification test. Leggett–Garg inequalities [1] are precisely designed for this: they test macrorealism + noninvasive measurability directly on a two-time-correlation observable of a single physical system, with loophole-closing precedents in superconducting circuits [2, 6], photons [3], and diamond NV centers [4]. A temporal Bell/CHSH variant [19, 20] supplies the complementary bound 2√2. Our contribution is a decision-theoretic translation of these bounds into a channel-electrophysiology + 2D-IR protocol with pre-specified classical null models and full SI-unit tracing.

**Target estimand / theoretical construct / operational proxy (three-level distinction):**
- **Target Estimand**: the true K₃ of the selectivity-filter "flip" observable Q(t) at 310 K.
- **Theoretical Construct**: K₃^QM(Ω, Γ), the LGI parameter under channel vibrational frequency spectrum Ω and decoherence kernel Γ.
- **Operational Proxy**: K̂₃ from weak degenerate measurements with 2D-IR readout [11], with NIM bias b_NIM subtracted.
